clues: This is a town in the far north of South Australia. It sits a long way north of Adelaide.
The days get so scorching hot here that people build homes under the ground. They live below ground to escape the heat.
In 1975, local Aboriginal people adopted a new name for the town. The same word is their name for the mulga tree.
This town is called the opal capital of the world. That is because of the huge amount of precious opals mined here.
A blower truck stands raised above the town sign. It shows how much opal mining shaped this place.
